contents.html: The Validated Products List (VPL) identifies information technology products that have been tested for conformance to Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) in accordance with Computer Systems Laboratory (CSL) conformance testing procedures, and have a current validation certificate or registered test report. The VPL also contains information about the organizations, test methods and procedures that support the validation programs for the FIPS identified in this document. The VPL includes computer language processors for programming languages COBOL, Fortran, Ada, Pascal, C, M[UMPS], and database language SQL; computer graphic implementations for GKS, CGM, PHIGS, and Raster Graphics; operating system implementations for POSIX; Open Systems Interconnection implementations; computer security implementations for DES, MAC and Key Management, product data implementations for IGES, and Open System Interconnection (OSI) implementations. The testing of products to assure conformance to the FIPS may be required by Government agencies in accordance with the FIPS, Federal Information Resources management Regulation (FIRMR) Parts 201.13 and 201.39, and the associated Federal ADP and Telecommunications Standards Index. The VPL is updated and published quarterly.
contents.html_ja: 検証済み製品リスト（VPL: Validated Products List）は、コンピューターシステム研究所（CSL）の適合性試験手順に従って連邦情報処理標準（FIPS）への適合性が試験され、現行の検証証明書または登録済み試験報告書を持つ情報技術製品を示すものです。VPL には、本書で示す FIPS の検証プログラムを支える組織、試験方法および手順に関する情報も含まれています。VPL には、プログラミング言語 COBOL、Fortran、Ada、Pascal、C、M[UMPS] およびデータベース言語 SQL のコンピューター言語処理系、GKS、CGM、PHIGS およびラスターグラフィックスの実装、POSIX のオペレーティングシステム実装、Open Systems Interconnection の実装、DES、MAC および鍵管理のコンピューターセキュリティ実装、IGES の製品データ実装、ならびに Open System Interconnection（OSI）の実装が含まれます。FIPS、連邦情報資源管理規則（FIRMR）第201.13部および第201.39部、ならびに関連する Federal ADP and Telecommunications Standards Index に従い、政府機関は、FIPSへの適合を保証するため製品試験を要求される場合があります。VPL は四半期ごとに更新・発行されます。

contents.html: The testing of Information Technology (IT) Products to determine the degree to which they conform to specific Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) may be required by Government agencies as specified by the FIPS, Federal Information Resources Management Regulation (FIRMR) Parts 201-20.303, 201-20.304, and 201-39.1002, and the associated Federal ADP and Telecommunications Standards Index. Products having a current validation certificate or test report may be offered or delivered by vendors in response to requirements as set forth in solicitations by Federal agencies. The Validated Products List (VPL) contains conformance testing information for the following IT Standards:
contents.html_ja: 情報技術（IT）製品が特定の連邦情報処理標準（FIPS）にどの程度適合しているかを判定する試験は、FIPS、連邦情報資源管理規則（FIRMR）の第 201-20.303 部、第 201-20.304 部および第 201-39.1002 部、ならびに関連する Federal ADP and Telecommunications Standards Index の定めにより、政府機関から求められる場合があります。現行の検証証明書または試験報告書を持つ製品は、連邦機関の調達要求に応じて、ベンダーが提供または納入することができます。検証済み製品リスト（VPL）には、次の IT 標準に関する適合性試験情報が含まれています。

contents.html: The organizations listed below have performed validations, supplied information, or are sources for Validation Summary Reports (VSR) for programming languages. These organizations may be contacted for validation information and for copies of VSR(s). COBOL and Fortran VSR(s) may be obtained from NIST. Pascal VSR(s) whose VSR numbers begin with "NIST" or end in "US" may also be obtained from NIST. Pascal VSR(s) whose VSR numbers end in "UK" are available from BSI. Ada VSR(s) may be obtained from the Ada Information Clearinghouse, the National Technical Information Service, or from the Ada Validation Facility (AVF) that produced the VSR. To obtain a copy of a VSR from an AVF, locate the upper case letter in the certificate number (e.g., 870608W1. . .). That letter corresponds to the letter in the CODE column to the left of the organizations listed below.
contents.html_ja: 以下に挙げる組織は、プログラミング言語の検証を実施したか、情報を提供したか、検証概要報告書（VSR）の入手元です。検証に関する情報や VSR の写しについては、これらの組織に問い合わせることができます。COBOL と Fortran の VSR は NIST から入手できます。VSR 番号が "NIST" で始まるか "US" で終わる Pascal の VSR も NIST から入手できます。VSR 番号が "UK" で終わる Pascal の VSR は BSI から入手できます。Ada の VSR は、Ada Information Clearinghouse、National Technical Information Service、またはその VSR を作成した Ada 検証機関（AVF）から入手できます。AVF から VSR の写しを入手するには、証明書番号（例: 870608W1. . .）の中の大文字を探してください。その文字は、以下に挙げる組織の左にある CODE 列の文字に対応します。

contents.html: The list of Ada compilers that have been validated by the Ada Joint Program Office (AJPO) is available in electronic form on the AdaIC Bulletin Board as file VALPROC.HLP. Access to the menu-driven bulletin board requires a computer terminal or personal computer and modem. Users should set their telecommunications package with the following parameters: Baud rate= 300 - 9600 baud; Data Bits= 8; Parity= none; Stop Bits= 1. Then dial 703/614-0215 (Commercial) or 224-0215 (Autovon). First-time users will be prompted to register for an account.
contents.html_ja: Ada Joint Program Office（AJPO）が検証した Ada コンパイラーのリストは、AdaIC Bulletin Board 上に VALPROC.HLP というファイルとして電子的な形式で公開されています。メニュー方式のこの電子掲示板を利用するには、コンピューター端末またはパーソナルコンピューターとモデムが必要です。利用者は通信ソフトウェアを次のパラメーターに設定してください。通信速度 = 300〜9600 ボー、データビット = 8、パリティ = なし、ストップビット = 1。その後、703/614-0215（一般回線）または 224-0215（Autovon）に発信します。初めての利用者には、アカウントの登録が求められます。

The product is listed to assist users in planning for future procurements. The term "Vendor-Tested Port" means the Vendor has complied with CSL procedures for self-testing a ported version of a registered SQL processor. NIST has reviewed Vendor test results and determined them to be equivalent to those in the referenced BASE VSR.

contents.html: The last column entries column include other hardware and operating system environments in which the processor operates, and the programming language compilers that interface with the SQL processor. The listings of the compilers and operating systems may contain a range of versions that are supported. Rebadged or renamed software are also listed here. This column is restricted to binary-compatible hardware environments. This column also lists the number and type of nonconformities for each programming language interface tested. "Schema" nonconformities are deficiencies in support for standard schema definition language constructs. "FIPS Flagger" in this column indicates that the mandatory FIPS Flagger requirement of FIPS 127 was not implemented. Refer to the VSR for details. The number of nonconformities is only one limited measure of the quality of an SQL interface. It is more important to analyze the nature of each individual nonconformity and its impact on meeting user requirements.
contents.html_ja: 最後の列の項目には、処理系が動作する他のハードウェアおよびオペレーティングシステムの環境と、SQL 処理系とインターフェースするプログラミング言語コンパイラーが含まれます。コンパイラーとオペレーティングシステムの一覧には、サポートされるバージョンの範囲が含まれることがあります。ブランド名を付け替えたソフトウェアや名称を変更したソフトウェアもここに掲載されます。この列は、バイナリ互換のハードウェア環境に限られます。この列には、試験された各プログラミング言語インターフェースについて、不適合の数と種類も掲載されます。"Schema" の不適合は、標準のスキーマ定義言語の構文要素のサポートにおける欠陥です。この列の "FIPS Flagger" は、FIPS 127 の必須要件である FIPS Flagger が実装されていないことを示します。詳細は VSR を参照してください。不適合の数は、SQL インターフェースの品質を測る限定的な尺度の 1 つにすぎません。個々の不適合の性質と、それが利用者の要件を満たすうえで及ぼす影響を分析することの方が重要です。

contents.html: The Graphical Kernel System (GKS) is a two-dimensional graphics tool box which provides for the display and manipulation of pictures and graphical input from the operator. The purpose of GKS is to promote portability of graphics applications for use on a variety of graphics workstations. It provides a functional interface between an application program and a configuration of graphical devices. The interface is at such a level of abstraction that hardware peculiarities are shielded from the application program.
contents.html_ja: Graphical Kernel System（GKS）は、絵の表示と操作、および操作者からのグラフィック入力を提供する 2 次元グラフィックスのツールボックスです。GKS の目的は、さまざまなグラフィックスワークステーションで使用するグラフィックスアプリケーションの可搬性を促進することです。GKS は、アプリケーションプログラムとグラフィックデバイスの構成との間の機能インターフェースを提供します。このインターフェースは、ハードウェア固有の癖がアプリケーションプログラムから隠される抽象化の水準にあります。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。OCR の文字を原本画像と語ごとに照合。原本p49: 段落

contents.html: FIPS PUB 120-1, GKS, is the first Federal Information Processing Standard Publication (FIPS PUB) registered for computer graphics systems. In accordance with FIPS PUB 120-1, two-dimensional graphics toolbox packages acquired for Federal use after November 3, 1986 should implement FIPS GKS. Conformance testing of GKS implementations protects Federal investment by ensuring adherence to the graphics standard. FIPS PUB 120-1 requires that GKS implementations offered to Federal agencies be tested using the NIST Test Suite to ensure that a particular implementation meets the specifications of the FIPS. The GKS Validation Test Suite (Fortran) is available from:
contents.html_ja: FIPS PUB 120-1 GKS は、コンピューターグラフィックスシステムについて登録された最初の連邦情報処理標準刊行物（FIPS PUB）です。FIPS PUB 120-1 に従い、1986 年 11 月 3 日以降に連邦で使用するために取得される 2 次元グラフィックスのツールボックスパッケージは、FIPS GKS を実装すべきです。GKS 実装の適合性試験は、グラフィックス標準への準拠を確実にすることで、連邦の投資を保護します。FIPS PUB 120-1 は、連邦機関に提供される GKS 実装について、特定の実装が FIPS の仕様を満たすことを確実にするため、NIST Test Suite を用いて試験することを求めています。GKS Validation Test Suite（Fortran）は次から入手できます。

contents.html: PHIGS stands for Programmer’s Hierarchical Interactive Graphics System. PHIGS is a system for interactive 3-dimensional (3D) graphics applications that provides programmers with a set of features enabling them to manipulate and display complex 3D objects. It is called hierarchical because the complex objects can be built up from simpler objects. PHIGS also provides a rich set of facilities for real-time interaction with the user. While it borrows many concepts from the Graphical Kernel System (GKS) standard, it also introduces many new features, such as a "graphics data base" (the centralized structure store), and support for modeling and viewing.
contents.html_ja: PHIGS は Programmer’s Hierarchical Interactive Graphics System の略です。PHIGS は、対話型の 3 次元（3D）グラフィックスアプリケーションのためのシステムで、複雑な 3D オブジェクトの操作と表示を可能にする一連の機能をプログラマーに提供します。複雑なオブジェクトを、より単純なオブジェクトから組み上げることができるため、階層型と呼ばれます。PHIGS はまた、利用者とのリアルタイムの対話のための豊富な機能も提供します。Graphical Kernel System（GKS）標準から多くの概念を借りている一方、"graphics data base"（集中型のストラクチャストア）や、モデリングおよびビューイングのサポートなど、多くの新しい機能も導入しています。

contents.html: Federal Information Processing Standard Publication (FIPS PUB) 128-1, Computer Graphics Metafile (CGM), is a data interchange standard for the storage and retrieval of picture information in a device independent manner. The purpose of the CGM is to facilitate the transfer of graphical information among different computer systems, graphical devices, and/or applications.
contents.html_ja: 連邦情報処理標準刊行物（FIPS PUB）128-1 Computer Graphics Metafile（CGM）は、画像情報をデバイスに依存しない方法で保存および取り出すためのデータ交換標準です。CGM の目的は、異なるコンピューターシステム、グラフィックデバイス、またはアプリケーションの間で、グラフィック情報の転送を容易にすることです。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。OCR の文字を原本画像と語ごとに照合。原本p50: 1段落。文字層で分かれた「CGM」を「the CGM is」の位置に戻す

contents.html: The FIPS PUB 128-1 requires the use of application profiles. In particular, FIPS PUB 128-1 requires the use of military specification MIL-D-28003A, commonly known as the Continuous Acquisition and Life-Cycle Support (CALS) CGM Application Profile (AP).
contents.html_ja: FIPS PUB 128-1 は、アプリケーションプロファイルの使用を求めています。特に、軍事仕様 MIL-D-28003A、通称 Continuous Acquisition and Life-Cycle Support（CALS）CGM Application Profile（AP）の使用を求めています。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。OCR の文字を原本画像と語ごとに照合。原本p50: 1段落。文字層で分かれた「CGM」を「(CALS) CGM Application Profile」の位置に戻す

contents.html: The NIST CGM Validation Test Service is divided into three testing programs: metafile, generator, and interpreter testing. The purpose of the Test Service is to determine the degree to which the metafile, CGM generator, or CGM interpreter conforms to the FIPS 128-1. Presently, the NIST CGM Validation Test Service addresses only CGM Version 1.
contents.html_ja: NIST CGM Validation Test Service は、メタファイル試験、ジェネレーター試験、インタープリター試験の 3 つの試験プログラムに分かれています。この Test Service の目的は、メタファイル、CGM ジェネレーター、または CGM インタープリターが FIPS 128-1 にどの程度適合しているかを判定することです。現在のところ、NIST CGM Validation Test Service は CGM Version 1 のみを対象としています。

contents.html: FIPS PUB 150 adopts EIA-538 which defines the facsimile coding schemes and their control functions for Group 4 facsimile apparatus, i.e., ITU-T (formerly CCITT) Recommendation T.6. It defines a standard compression algorithm (T.6 - Group 4) suitable for the storage, retrieval, and interchange of raster graphics images.
contents.html_ja: FIPS PUB 150 は EIA-538 を採用しています。EIA-538 は、Group 4 ファクシミリ装置のファクシミリ符号化方式とその制御機能、すなわち ITU-T（旧 CCITT）勧告 T.6 を定義しています。EIA-538 は、ラスターグラフィックス画像の保存、取り出しおよび交換に適した標準の圧縮アルゴリズム（T.6 - Group 4）を定義しています。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。OCR の文字を原本画像と語ごとに照合。原本p51: 段落。OCR の「CC11T )」は「CCITT)」

contents.html: Military Specification MIL-R-28002 specifies the structure and encoding of raster data files to be delivered to the government. It specifies the use of the standard compression algorithm defined in FIPS PUB 150. It also specifies the use of standard file headers which are defined in MIL-STD-1840. MIL-STD-1840 standardizes the format and structure of digital technical data files for the purpose of interchange between organizations or systems.
contents.html_ja: 軍事仕様 MIL-R-28002 は、政府に納入されるラスターデータファイルの構造と符号化を規定しています。MIL-R-28002 は、FIPS PUB 150 で定義された標準の圧縮アルゴリズムの使用を規定しており、MIL-STD-1840 で定義された標準のファイルヘッダーの使用も規定しています。MIL-STD-1840 は、組織間またはシステム間で交換するためのデジタル技術データファイルの形式と構造を標準化しています。

contents.html: The National Institute of Standards and Technology through its Computer Systems Laboratory (NIST/CSL) has established a conformance testing program for the Federal Information Standard for POSIX (FIPS 151-1 and FIPS 151-2). FIPS 151-2 replaced FIPS 151-1 in its entirely on October 15, 1993. These standards are based on the IEEE POSIX Std. 1003.1-1988 (FIPS 151-1) and ISO/IEC 9945-1:1990 (FIPS 151-2). The testing model includes a Certification Authority, NVLAP Accredited Testing Laboratories, Clients and the official NIST POSIX Conformance Test Suites. The Certification Authority is the Director of NIST/CSL. The National Voluntary Laboratory Accreditation Program (NVLAP), part of NIST, accredits the testing laboratories. The test suites NIST-PCTS:151-1 and NIST-PCTS:151-2 were developed by NIST/CSL and are based on the test assertions specified by the IEEE Standard for Information Technology — Test Methods for Measuring Conformance to POSIX, IEEE Std. 1003.3-1991 (NIST-PCTS:151-1) and the IEEE Standard for Information Technology — Test Methods for Measuring conformance to POSIX.1, IEEE Std 2003.1-1992 (NIST-PCTS:151-2).
contents.html_ja: 国立標準技術研究所は、そのコンピューターシステム研究所（NIST/CSL）を通じて、POSIX に関する連邦情報標準（FIPS 151-1 および FIPS 151-2）の適合性試験プログラムを設けています。FIPS 151-2 は、1993 年 10 月 15 日に FIPS 151-1 を全面的に置き換えました。これらの標準は、IEEE POSIX Std. 1003.1-1988（FIPS 151-1）および ISO/IEC 9945-1:1990（FIPS 151-2）に基づいています。試験モデルは、認証機関（Certification Authority）、NVLAP 認定試験所、依頼者、および NIST の公式 POSIX 適合性試験スイートで構成されます。認証機関は NIST/CSL の所長です。NIST の一部である National Voluntary Laboratory Accreditation Program（NVLAP）が試験所を認定します。試験スイート NIST-PCTS:151-1 および NIST-PCTS:151-2 は NIST/CSL が開発したもので、それぞれ IEEE Standard for Information Technology — Test Methods for Measuring Conformance to POSIX, IEEE Std. 1003.3-1991（NIST-PCTS:151-1）および IEEE Standard for Information Technology — Test Methods for Measuring conformance to POSIX.1, IEEE Std 2003.1-1992（NIST-PCTS:151-2）に規定された試験アサーションに基づいています。

contents.html: There are Accredited POSIX Testing Laboratories (APTLs) accredited by NVLAP for using one or both test suites. NVLAP accreditation is renewable after one year, and identifies the specific testing procedures which the lab is authorized to run. The labs provide testing and analysis services to their clients and may forward the final test results to NIST/CSL for evaluation and subsequent issuance of a Certificate of Validation by NIST/CSL.
contents.html_ja: 一方または両方の試験スイートを使用するために NVLAP から認定された Accredited POSIX Testing Laboratories（APTL）があります。NVLAP の認定は 1 年後に更新でき、その試験所が実施を認められた具体的な試験手順を特定します。試験所は、依頼者に試験および分析のサービスを提供し、最終的な試験結果を NIST/CSL に送付して、評価と、その後の NIST/CSL による検証証明書の発行を受けることができます。

contents.html: Testing policy documents and registers of validated products and accredited laboratories and available on an electronic mail (email) file server system. For most email systems, send an email message to posix@nist.gov (mail posix@nist.gov). The first line of the message should contain a command to send index (send posix/index). After issuing the send command and a carriage return, end the email message. A listing of all of the available files will be returned via email to the requesting email address.
contents.html_ja: 試験方針の文書、ならびに検証済み製品および認定試験所の登録簿は、電子メール（email）のファイルサーバーシステムで入手できます。ほとんどの電子メールシステムでは、posix@nist.gov 宛てに電子メールを送ります（mail posix@nist.gov）。メッセージの 1 行目には、索引の送信を要求するコマンドを書きます（send posix/index）。send コマンドと復帰改行を送信した後、電子メールメッセージを終了します。利用可能なすべてのファイルの一覧が、依頼者の電子メールアドレスに電子メールで返送されます。

contents.html: An accredited lab may submit a "clean" test report to NIST/CSL for evaluation in anticipation of a Certification of Validation being issued. "Clean" implies no test assertion failures. The Certificate of Validation will confirm that the stated product has been tested using the official NIST-PCTS and that the test results have been validated by NIST/CSL. The Certificate of Validation and the Test Results Summary contain information on the product tested, the implementation that was tested, the suppliers, conditional features that were tested, configuration details and the identification of the testing laboratory. These certificates are issued by NIST/CSL through the testing lab. Fees for services by the testing labs are established by the labs.
contents.html_ja: 認定試験所は、検証証明書が発行されることを見込んで、"clean" な試験報告書を NIST/CSL に提出して評価を受けることができます。"Clean" とは、試験アサーションの失敗がないことを意味します。検証証明書は、示された製品が公式の NIST-PCTS を用いて試験され、その試験結果が NIST/CSL によって検証されたことを確認するものです。検証証明書と Test Results Summary には、試験された製品、試験された実装、サプライヤー、試験された条件付き機能、構成の詳細、および試験所の識別に関する情報が含まれます。これらの証明書は、NIST/CSL が試験所を通じて発行します。試験所のサービスの料金は、試験所が定めます。

contents.html: The following products have been tested by an Accredited POSIX Testing Laboratory (APTL) using the official National Institute of Standards and Technology POSIX Conformance Test Suite (NIST-PCTS:151-2) for the Federal Information Processing Standards 151-2 (FIPS PUB 151-2). contents.html_ja: 次の製品は、連邦情報処理標準 151-2（FIPS PUB 151-2）について、国立標準技術研究所の公式の POSIX Conformance Test Suite（NIST-PCTS:151-2）を用いて、Accredited POSIX Testing Laboratory（APTL）が試験したものです。検証証明書は NIST/CSL が発行しています。サポートされる条件付き機能、構成の詳細、解決された試験コード（該当する場合）に関する追加情報は、NIST/CSL から入手できます。

contents.html: Information in this listing includes product information on the implementation, system tested and type of implementation. FIPS 151-2 supports three types of implementations, native, hosted, and cooperating. A native implementation "refers to an implementation of POSIX.1 that interfaces directly to an operating system kernel." A cooperating implementation "refers to an implementation of POSIX.1 that interfaces directly to an operating system kernel but the load modules are not produceable on this implementation." A hosted implementation "referes to an implementation of POSIX.1 that is accomplished through interfaces from the POSIX.1 services to some alternate form of operating system kernel services."
contents.html_ja: この一覧の情報には、実装に関する製品情報、試験されたシステム、および実装の種類が含まれます。FIPS 151-2 は、ネイティブ（native）、ホスト型（hosted）、協調型（cooperating）の 3 種類の実装をサポートしています。ネイティブ実装とは、「オペレーティングシステムカーネルと直接インターフェースする POSIX.1 の実装」を指します。協調型実装とは、「オペレーティングシステムカーネルと直接インターフェースしますが、この実装上ではロードモジュールを生成できない POSIX.1 の実装」を指します。ホスト型実装とは、「POSIX.1 サービスからオペレーティングシステムカーネルサービスの何らかの代替形態へのインターフェースを通じて実現される POSIX.1 の実装」を指します。

contents.html: This register is also available on an electronic mail (email) file server system. To use the service, you must be able to send and receive email via the Internet. For most email systems, send an email message (mail posix@nist.gov) with the first line of the message containing a command to send 151-2req and a carriage return. The next line should simply end your email message (on some systems a period and a carriage return). This register will be returned via email to your email address. There is also a register for FIPS 151-1 accredited laboratories and validated products. For this register use the command send 151-1req.
contents.html_ja: この登録簿は、電子メール（email）のファイルサーバーシステムでも入手できます。このサービスを利用するには、インターネット経由で電子メールを送受信できる必要があります。ほとんどの電子メールシステムでは、メール（mail posix@nist.gov）を送り、メッセージの1行目に send 151-2req コマンドと復帰文字を入れます。次の行では、電子メールメッセージを終了するだけにします（一部のシステムではピリオドと復帰文字を入れます）。この登録簿は、依頼者の電子メールアドレス宛てに電子メールで返送されます。FIPS 151-1 の認定試験所と検証済み製品の登録簿もあります。この登録簿を入手するには send 151-1req コマンドを使います。

contents.html: FIPS PUB 46-2 specifies a cryptographic algorithm that converts plaintext to ciphertext using a 56-bit key. Testing procedures for the validation of devices as conforming to FIPS PUB 46-2 are described in the NBS Special Publication 500-20, Validating the Correctness of Hardware Implementations of the NBS Data Encryption Standard. The validation of a device is performed by running the Monte Carlo test described in the publication. The Monte-Carlo test consists of eight million encryptions and four million decryptions, with two encryptions and one decryption making up a single test. The test is designed to use the Electronic Codebook Mode (ECB) of DES. Although the actual test described in NBS Special Publication 500-20 is the same test used to validate devices today, the procedures for administering the test have changed. Currently, the test is performed by the vendor using initial values supplied by NIST. The vendor uses the supplied information to run the Monte-Carlo test and sends the results to NIST.
contents.html_ja: FIPS PUB 46-2 は、56 ビットの鍵を用いて平文を暗号文に変換する暗号アルゴリズムを規定しています。デバイスが FIPS PUB 46-2 に適合していることを検証するための試験手順は、NBS Special Publication 500-20 Validating the Correctness of Hardware Implementations of the NBS Data Encryption Standard に記載されています。デバイスの検証は、この刊行物に記載されたモンテカルロ試験を実行して行います。モンテカルロ試験は、800 万回の暗号化と 400 万回の復号で構成され、2 回の暗号化と 1 回の復号で 1 つの試験を構成します。この試験は、DES の Electronic Codebook Mode（ECB）を使用するように設計されています。NBS Special Publication 500-20 に記載された実際の試験は、現在デバイスの検証に使われている試験と同じですが、試験を実施する手順は変更されています。現在、試験はベンダーが NIST から提供された初期値を用いて行います。ベンダーは、提供された情報を用いてモンテカルロ試験を実行し、その結果を NIST に送付します。

contents.html: FIPS PUB 113, Computer Data Authentication, specifies a Data Encryption Algorithm which may be used to detect unauthorized intentional and accidental modifications to data. This process is known as data authentication. The algorithm is based on DES and is used to authenticate an entire binary message. FIPS PUB 113 is compatible with ANSI X9.9 which provides methods for authenticating an entire binary message as well as all or parts of a message which are in a coded character format. Procedures for the validation of products which implement FIPS PUB 113 and ANSI X9.9 are described in NBS Special Publication 500-156, Message Authentication Code (MAC) Validation System: Requirements and Procedures.
contents.html_ja: FIPS PUB 113 Computer Data Authentication は、データに対する意図的または偶発的な不正変更を検出するために使用できる Data Encryption Algorithm を規定しています。この処理は、データ認証と呼ばれます。このアルゴリズムは DES に基づいており、バイナリメッセージ全体の認証に使用されます。FIPS PUB 113 は ANSI X9.9 と互換性があり、ANSI X9.9 は、バイナリメッセージ全体の認証に加えて、符号化された文字形式のメッセージの全体または一部を認証する方法も提供します。FIPS PUB 113 と ANSI X9.9 を実装する製品の検証手順は、NBS Special Publication 500-156 Message Authentication Code (MAC) Validation System: Requirements and Procedures に記載されています。

contents.html: FIPS PUB 171 adopts ANSI X9.17 for Federal Government use. ANSI X9.17, Financial Institution Key Management (Wholesale), provides procedures and protocols for the secure generation, distribution, storage, entry, use and destruction of symmetric cryptographic keying material (e.g., DES). It provides key management solutions for a variety of operational environments, and as such, ANSI X9.17 contains a number of options. FIPS PUB 171 specifies a particular set of options whenever keying material is distributed using the protocols of ANSI X9.17. Procedures for the validation of products which conform to a subset of the options selected in FIPS PUB 171 are described in the Key Management Validation System: Point-to-Point Validation System document which is available from the Manager of the Security Group (see Section 6.5).
contents.html_ja: FIPS PUB 171 は、連邦政府で使用するために ANSI X9.17 を採用しています。ANSI X9.17 Financial Institution Key Management (Wholesale) は、共通鍵暗号の鍵素材（例: DES）の安全な生成、配布、保管、入力、使用および破棄のための手順とプロトコルを提供します。ANSI X9.17 はさまざまな運用環境に対する鍵管理の解決策を提供するため、多くのオプションを含んでいます。FIPS PUB 171 は、ANSI X9.17 のプロトコルを用いて鍵素材を配布する場合の特定のオプションの組を規定しています。FIPS PUB 171 で選択されたオプションの一部に適合する製品の検証手順は、Key Management Validation System: Point-to-Point Validation System 文書に記載されており、この文書は Manager of the Security Group（第 6.5 節を参照）から入手できます。

contents.html: FIPS 177, Initial Graphics Exchange Specifications (IGES) defines a neutral file format for the exchange of product model data and representation among differing computer-aided design and computer-aided manufacturing (CAD/CAM) systems. FIPS 177 adopts the ASME/ANSI Y14.26M, IGES version 4.0.
contents.html_ja: FIPS 177 Initial Graphics Exchange Specifications（IGES）は、異なるコンピューター支援設計・コンピューター支援製造（CAD/CAM）システムの間で、製品モデルのデータと表現を交換するための中立なファイル形式を定義しています。FIPS 177 は、ASME/ANSI Y14.26M の IGES version 4.0 を採用しています。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。OCR の文字を原本画像と語ごとに照合。原本p103: 段落

contents.html: A revision to FIPS 177-1 (announced in Federal Register, April 12, 1995) will adopt the ANSI/US PRO 100 IGES, version 5.2. In accordance with FIPS 177-1, CAD/CAM systems acquired for Federal use shall include an IGES preprocessor and postprocessor capability. FIPS 177-1 requires that IGES implementations offered to Federal agencies be tested using the NIST IGES validation test suite. Conformance testing of IGES implementations protects Federal investments by ensuring adherence to the IGES specification and maximizing the probability of successful exchange among systems which implement IGES. The NIST IGES test procedures and test suites are available from:
contents.html_ja: FIPS 177-1 の改訂（1995 年 4 月 12 日の Federal Register で告知）では、ANSI/US PRO 100 IGES の version 5.2 が採用される予定です。FIPS 177-1 に従い、連邦で使用するために取得される CAD/CAM システムは、IGES のプリプロセッサーおよびポストプロセッサーの機能を備えなければなりません。FIPS 177-1 は、連邦機関に提供される IGES 実装について、NIST IGES 検証試験スイートを用いて試験することを求めています。IGES 実装の適合性試験は、IGES 仕様への準拠を確実にし、IGES を実装するシステム間での交換が成功する確率を最大にすることで、連邦の投資を保護します。NIST の IGES 試験手順および試験スイートは、次から入手できます。

contents.html: The NIST IGES Validation Test service tests preprocessors and/or postprocessors for conformance to either IGES 4.0, IGES 5.2, or MIL-D-28000, Class II. Preprocessors and postprocessors are tested separately, using different test suites. A certificate of validation is issued for those processors that have been tested and are considered to be in compliance with FIPS 177. A registered report without certificate is issued for those processors that have been tested but contain errors.
contents.html_ja: NIST IGES Validation Test サービスは、プリプロセッサーまたはポストプロセッサー（あるいはその両方）が、IGES 4.0、IGES 5.2、または MIL-D-28000 Class II のいずれかに適合しているかどうかを試験します。プリプロセッサーとポストプロセッサーは、異なる試験スイートを用いて別々に試験されます。検証証明書は、試験を受け、FIPS 177 に適合していると見なされる処理系に対して発行されます。試験を受けたものの誤りを含む処理系には、証明書のない登録済み報告書が発行されます。

contents.html: The Open System Interconnection (OSI) products database was started to assist Federal Agencies in assuring conformance to Federal Information Processing Standard 146-1, Government Open Systems Interconnection Profile (GOSIP). FIPS 146-1 has been replaced by FIPS 146-2, Profiles for Open Systems Internetworking Technologies, (POSIT). However, a register of OSI products is maintained for the convenience of those agencies that wish to acquire products based on OSI standards. Testing for conformance to the OSI standards and for interoperability with other OSI implementations is available.
contents.html_ja: 開放型システム間相互接続（OSI）製品データベースは、連邦機関が連邦情報処理標準 146-1 Government Open Systems Interconnection Profile（GOSIP）への適合を確実にするのを支援するために開始されました。FIPS 146-1 は、FIPS 146-2 Profiles for Open Systems Internetworking Technologies（POSIT）に置き換えられました。ただし、OSI 標準に基づく製品の取得を希望する機関の便宜のため、OSI 製品の登録簿は維持されています。OSI 標準への適合性と、他の OSI 実装との相互運用性の試験を利用できます。

DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE U.S. Technology Administration National Institute of Standards and Technology Computer Systems Laboratory Software Standards Validation Group Gaithersburg, MD 20899
U.S. DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE Ronald H. Brown, Secretary TECHNOLOGY ADMINISTRATION Mary L. Good, Under Secretary for Technology NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF STANDARDS AND TECHNOLOGY Arati Prabhakar, Director

The Validated Products List (VPL) identifies information technology products that have been tested for conformance to Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) in accordance with Computer Systems Laboratory (CSL) conformance testing procedures, and have a current validation certificate or registered test report. The VPL also contains information about the organizations, test methods and procedures that support the validation programs for the FIPS identified in this document. The VPL includes computer language processors for programming languages COBOL, Fortran, Ada, Pascal, C, M[UMPS], and database language SQL; computer graphic implementations for GKS, CGM, PHIGS, and Raster Graphics; operating system implementations for POSIX; Open Systems Interconnection implementations; computer

security implementations for DES, and Key Management, product data implementations for IGES, and Open System Interconnection (OSI) implementations. The testing of products to assure conformance to the FIPS may be required by Government agencies in accordance with the FIPS, Federal Information Resources management Regulation (FIRMR) Parts 201.13 and 201.39, and the associated Federal ADP and Telecommunications Standards Index. The VPL is updated and published quarterly.
The co-editors would like to acknowledge the valuable efforts and contributions of the following people and organizations within NIST.
Judy Kailey, (ISE) for developing the document layout, and editing previous issues of the VPL.
William Dashiell, (ISE) for Ada and SQL entries.
Lynne Rosenthal, (ISE), for CGM and IGES entries.
Martha Gray, of the Systems and Software Technology Division, CSL, for the POSIX entries.
James Foti, of the Computer Security Division, CSL, for the Computer Security entries.
Michele Buckley, of the Systems and Network Architecture Division, CSL, for Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) entries.

3.2 Organization of Database Language Processor Entries

APPENDIX A FIPS CONFORMANCE TESTING PRODUCTS AND SERVICES

The testing of Information Technology (IT) Products to determine the degree to which they conform to specific Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) may be required by Government agencies as specified by the FIPS, Federal Information Resources Management Regulation (FIRMR) Parts 201-20.303, 201-20.304, and 201-39.1002, and the associated Federal ADP and Telecommunications Standards Index. Products having a current validation certificate or test report may be offered or delivered by vendors in response to requirements as set forth in solicitations by Federal agencies. The Validated Products List (VPL) contains conformance testing information for the following IT Standards:
Programming Languages COBOL, Fortran, Ada, Pascal, C, and M[UMPS] Database Language SQL Graphics POSIX Computer Security Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) Product Data (IGES)

This List is updated and published quarterly. The information contained herein is supplied by the contributors listed in Section 2.6 and Appendix A, and is current as of the tenth of the month preceding the publication date. Copies of the VPL may be obtained from:
National Technical Information Service U.S. Department of Commerce 5285 Port Royal Road

The entries in the printed VPL (except those for Open Systems Interconnection (OSI), POSIX and Ada) are contained in WordPerfect Version 5.1 files and may be accessed on the Internet using the following instructions:

Section 2 identifies those COBOL, Fortran, Pascal, C, Ada, and M[UMPS] programming language processors that have a current validation certificate or registered test report referencing the applicable FIPS as of the date of this publication.
Section 3 identifies those SQL language processors that have a validation certificate or a registered test report for FIPS PUB 127-2 as of the date of this publication.
Section 4 lists the implementations or files for which a validation certificate is currently in place. These entries include:
Section 5 identifies POSIX products that have a current validation certificate for FIPS PUB 151-1 and FIPS PUB 151-2.

Section 6 contains information regarding validated products for FIPS PUB 46-1, Data Encryption Standard (DES), FIPS PUB 113, Computer Data Authentication (Implements Message Authentication Code, ANSI X9.9), and FIPS PUB 171, Key Management Using ANSI X9.17.
Section 7 contains information regarding validated products for FIPS PUB 177, Initial Graphics Exchange Specification (IGES).

Graphical Kernel System (GKS) implementations (FIPS PUB 120-1), Programmer’s Hierarchical Interactive Graphics Systems (PHIGS) (FIPS PUB 153), Computer Graphics Metafiles (CGMs) (FIPS PUB 128), Raster Graphics data files (FIPS PUB 150).
Section 8 contains information about the OSI Products Database which was developed for FIPS PUB 146-1 FIPS Pub 146-2, Profile for Open Systems Internetworking Technologies (POSIT), replaces FIPS
146-1. However, this information is retained for the convenience of agencies that wish to acquire OSI Protocols.
Appendix A lists FIPS conformance testing products and services available to the public. Information for these products and services may be obtained by contacting the appropriate person listed.

As specified by the FIPS, FIRMR and the associated Federal ADP and Telecommunications Standards Index, Federal agencies when acquiring language processors, are responsible for assuring that processors are in accordance with the following FIPS for programming languages:

a. COBOL processors must satisfy the provisions of FIPS PUB 21-3, COBOL, and must be identified as implementing all of the language elements of at least one of the subsets of FIPS COBOL as specified in FIPS PUB 21-3.
b. BASIC processors must satisfy the provisions of FIPS PUB 68-2, BASIC.

c. Fortran processors must satisfy the provision of FIPS PUB 69-1, Fortran, (based on ANSI X3.9-1978) and must be identified as implementing all of the language elements of the subset or full levels of FIPS Fortran as specified in FIPS PUB 69-1.
d. Pascal processors must satisfy the provisions of FIPS PUB 109, Pascal.
e. Ada processors must satisfy the provisions of FIPS PUB 119, Ada.
g. C processors must satisfy the provisions of FIPS PUB 160, C.
h. VHDL processors must satisfy the provisions of FIPS PUB 172, VHDL.
f. M[UMPS] processors must satisfy the provisions of FIPS PUB 125-1, M[UMPS],
Copies of the above publications are for sale by the National Technical Information Service, U.S. Department of Commerce, Springfield, VA 22161.
Conformance testing programs are currently available for all above FIPS except for the programming language BASIC and VHDL. A test suite for BASIC is being developed.
2.2 Organization of Programming Language Processor Entries
The entries in the VPL for programming language processors are presented as follows:
The SUPPLIER column contains the name of the provider of the processor that was tested.
The next column contains the PROCESSOR IDentification, the Validation Summary Report (VSR) number, the SUBSET, and the EXPIRY DATE.
The PROCESSOR ID is the product name and version of the processor that was tested.

The VSR number refers to the VSR that was produced as a result of the testing. The VSR describes the testing environment and details any processor nonconformity that was detected as a result of the testing. Information for obtaining a VSR is listed in section 2.6.

The EXPIRY DATE is the expiration date of the Certificate of Validation or Registered Validation Summary Report. A processor may be included in the List after the certificate has expired if the validation is in process. Notification must be received by NIST at least 30 days prior to publication of the List in order for such a processor to be included. In this case the expiration date will be followed by "(pending)".

For COBOL processors, the SUBSET refers to the applicable Federal Subset (Minimum, Intermediate, or High). For Fortran processors, the LEVEL specifies the applicable Federal level (Subset or Full). For Pascal processors, the ISO 7185 Pascal Standard Level (ISO 7185 Level 0 is equivalent to FIPS 109).
The HARDWARE & OPERATING SYSTEM column presents the hardware and operating system environment (including pertinent supporting system software) used during the validation.

The entries in the OTHER ENVIRONMENTS column are registered hardware and operating system environments for the processor tested. The vendor of the processor has certified that the identified processor, when operating under the environments included in this column, produces the same test results as those obtained from the hardware and operating system environment used during the validation. Test results and other information from these environments may be required as evidence for entries to be included in this column.
The entries for Ada language processors are not presented in column format.
Also listed are the programming language processors that have been tested and during the testing were found to have one or more nonconformities.

In accordance with the requirements referenced in Section 1.1, language processors offered to the Government for purchase, lease, or use in connection with ADP services shall be validated for confor-mance to FIPS for programming languages. To confirm that the specifications of the designated FIPS have been met:
a. the processor shall be tested with the Compiler Validation System (CVS) approved by NIST,
b. the processor validations shall be conducted in accordance with NIST validation procedures,
c. a Validation Summary Report (VSR) shall be produced summarizing the test results of the CVS on the designated processor for that FIPS,
d. all nonconformities noted in the VSR shall be corrected within twelve months,

e. a Certificate of Validation shall be issued if validation results warrant. In order for a processor to receive a Certificate of Validation the processor must successfully pass all applicable tests of the CVS without exception.

The Federal ADP and Telecommunications Standards Index supplies standard terminology which may allow for delayed validation. When delayed validation is allowed, the offeror may meet this requirement by showing evidence of having submitted the processor for validation. Proof of submission is in the form of a letter from NIST scheduling the validation.

Programming language processors offered to the Federal Government must comply with the applicable Government requirements. Failure to comply with these requirements shall be deemed sufficient cause to declare a bidder non-responsive or to declare a vendor in default for failure to deliver required software.
For a processor to be placed in the List it must:
a. have been officially tested within the past twelve calendar months, and
b. have no errors remaining that were identified during a previous test.
A processor is removed from the List when:
a. the processor is not officially tested within twelve calendar months, or
b. testing indicates that the processor still contains errors identified during a previous validation.
Validation procedures are published in the following documents:

Compiler Validation Procedures, dated January 15, 1993 Ada Compiler Validation Procedures and Guidelines, Version 3.1, August, 1992 Pascal Validation Policy and Procedures, Version 5.6, September 1, 1994 MfUMPS] Validation Procedures, Version 1.0, dated August 13, 1992

A Certificate of Validation is issued for those programming language processors that have been tested and are considered to be in compliance with the FIPS as specified by the FIPS, FIRMR and the associated Federal ADP and Telecommunications Index.
The requirement for retesting may be waived and the certificate of validation extended at the option of NIST
a. no errors were identified during the previous testing of the processor,
b. the vendor certifies, in writing, to NIST that no changes have been made to either the processor or the supporting system software, and
c. no new version of the validation system has been officially released during the interim period.

As specified by the FIPS, FIRMR and the associated Federal ADP and Telecommunications Standards Index, Federal agencies, when acquiring SQL processors, are responsible for assuring that processors are in 3.2 accordance with the applicable FIPS PUB 127, Database Language SQL. On December 3, 1993, FIPS PUB 127-2 superseded FIPS PUB 127-1.
Organization of Database Language Processor Entries
Each entry in the VPL is a very limited extract from the Validation Summary Report (VSR) available from the Software Standards Validation Group at NIST. See 3.4 and 3.5 below.

Products validated for conformance to FIPS PUB 127-2 are listed. Products that demonstrated one or more nonconformities, as assessed by the SQL Validation System, are listed separately at the end. (These products are considered "provisionally" validated, pending correction of nonconformities.) The entries in the VPL for database language processors are presented as follows:
The VENDOR column contains the name of the Vendor of the processor.

The second column contains the name of the processor, its version number, the VSR number, the Expiry date of the Validation Certificate or the Registered VSR, and the hardware and operating system on which the testing was done. The term "Pre-release" means that the vendor has designated the SQL processor as "not commercially available" at the time of validation. The product is listed to assist users in planning for future procurements. The term "Vendor-Tested Port" means the Vendor has complied with CSL procedures for self-testing a ported version of a registered SQL processor. NIST has reviewed Vendor test results and determined them to be equivalent to those in the referenced BASE VSR.

The INTERFACES & COMPILERS column contains the names of associated interactive SQL or programming language interfaces, and identification ofthe programming language compilers that interface with the SQL processor. A listing in the COMPILERS column is not an indication that the compiler has been validated for the applicable programming language standard. See the preceding "Programming Languages" Section for a list of validated compilers.

The last column entries column include other hardware and operating system environments in which the processor operates, and the programming language compilers that interface with the SQL processor. The listings of the compilers and operating systems may contain a range of versions that are supported. Rebadged or renamed software are also listed here. This column is restricted to binary-compatible hardware environments. This column also lists the number and type of nonconformities for each programming language interface tested. "Schema" nonconformities are deficiencies in support for standard schema definition language constructs. "FIPS Flagger" in this column indicates that the mandatory FIPS Flagger requirement of FIPS 127 was not implemented. Refer to the VSR for details. The number of nonconformities is only one limited measure of the quality of an SQL interface. It is more important to analyze the nature of each individual nonconformity and its impact on meeting user requirements.

Refer to Database Language SOL Validation Procedures. The requirements for validation of database language processors are the same as those for programming language processors, listed in section 2.3.1 with

several exceptions. Expired VSRs are deleted from the VPL to motivate vendors to test new releases of their SQL processors and to demonstrate conformance to more comprehensive versions of the SQL Test Suite. Information about expired VSRs or vendor self-testing with the SQL Test Suite may be available from the vendor.

A Certificate of Validation is issued for those SQL processors that have been tested and are considered to 3.5 be in compliance with FIPS as specified by the FIPS, by the FIRMR, and the associated Federal ADP and Telecommunications Standards Index.

A Validation Summary Report (VSR) that indicates that the SQL processors did not meet the criteria for a Certificate of Validation may be registered by the Computer Systems Laboratory. The Graphical Kernel System (GKS) is a two-dimensional graphics tool box which provides for the display and manipulation of pictures and graphical input from the operator. The purpose of GKS is to promote portability of graphics applications for use on a variety of graphics workstations. It provides a functional interface between an application program and a configuration of graphical devices. The interface is at such a level of abstraction that hardware peculiarities are shielded from the application program.

FIPS PUB 120-1, GKS, is the first Federal Information Processing Standard Publication (FIPS PUB) registered for computer graphics systems. In accordance with FIPS PUB 120-1, two-dimensional graphics toolbox packages acquired for Federal use after November 3, 1986 should implement FIPS GKS. Conformance testing of GKS implementations protects Federal investment by ensuring adherence to the graphics standard. FIPS PUB 120-1 requires that GKS implementations offered to Federal agencies be tested using the NIST Test Suite to ensure that a particular implementation meets the specifications of the FIPS. The GKS Validation Test Suite (Fortran) is available from:

PHIGS stands for Programmer’s Hierarchical Interactive Graphics System. PHIGS is a system for interactive 3-dimensional (3D) graphics applications that provides programmers with a set of features enabling them to manipulate and display complex 3D objects. It is called hierarchical because the complex objects can be built up from simpler objects. PHIGS also provides a rich set of facilities for real-time interaction with the user. While it borrows many concepts from the Graphical Kernel System (GKS) standard, it also introduces many new features, such as a "graphics data base" (the centralized structure store), and support for modeling and viewing.

In accordance with FIPS PUB 153, (PHIGS), 3D graphics packages acquired for Federal use should implement FIPS PHIGS. Conformance testing of PHIGS implementations protects Federal investment by ensuring adherence to the graphics standard. FIPS PUB 153 requires that PHIGS implementations offered to Federal agencies be tested using the NIST PVT (PHIGS Validation Tests) test suite. The test suite ensures that a particular implementation meets the specifications set forth in the FIPS. The PHIGS PVT test suite is available from:
Project Leader, PHIGS Validation Tests National Institute of Standards and Technology Computer Systems Laboratory Bldg. 225, Room A-266

FIPS PUB 150 adopts EIA-538 which defines the facsimile coding schemes and their control functions for Group 4 facsimile apparatus, i.e., ITU-T (formerly CC11T ) Recommendation T.6. It defines a standard compression algorithm (T.6 - Group 4) suitable for the storage, retrieval, and interchange of raster graphics images.

Military Specification MIL-R-28002 specifies the structure and encoding of raster data files to be delivered to the government. It specifies the use of the standard compression algorithm defined in FIPS PUB 150. It also specifies the use of standard file headers which are defined in MIL-STD-1840. MIL-STD-1840 standardizes the format and structure of digital technical data files for the purpose of interchange between organizations or systems.

The National Institute of Standards and Technology through its Computer Systems Laboratory (NIST/CSL) has established a conformance testing program for the Federal Information Standard for POSIX (FIPS 151-1 and FIPS 151-2). FIPS 151-2 replaced FIPS 151-1 in its entirely on October 15, 1993. These standards are based on the IEEE POSIX Std. 1003.1-1988 (FIPS 151-1) and ISO/IEC 9945-1:1990 (FIPS 151-2). The testing model includes a Certification Authority, NVLAP Accredited Testing Laboratories, Clients and the official NIST POSIX Conformance Test Suites. The Certification Authority is the Director of NIST/CSL. The National Voluntary Laboratory Accreditation Program (NVLAP), part of NIST, accredits the testing laboratories. The test suites NIST-PCTS: 151-1 and NIST-PCTS: 151-2 were developed by NIST/CSL and are based on the test assertions specified by the — IEEE Standard for Information Technology Test Methods for Measuring Conformance to POSIX,
IEEE Std. 1003.3-1991 (NIST-PCTS: 151-1) and the IEEE Standard for Information Technology Test Methods for Measuring conformance to POSIX. 1, IEEE Std 2003.1-1992 (NIST-PCTS: 151-2).
There are Accredited POSIX Testing Laboratories (APTLs) accredited by NVLAP for using one or both
accreditation is renewable after one year, and identifies the specific testing

An accredited lab may submit a "clean" test report to NIST/CSL for evaluation in anticipation of a Certification of Validation being issued. "Clean" implies no test assertion failures. The Certificate of Validation will confirm that the stated product has been tested using the official NIST-PCTS and that the test results have been validated by NIST/CSL. The Certificate of Validation and the Test Results Summary contain information on the product tested, the implementation that was tested, the suppliers, conditional features that were tested, configuration details and the identification of the testing laboratory. The lists in Sections 6.6, 6.7 and 6.8 provide technical information about products that have been validated as conforming to the following computer security FIPS:
a. Data Encryption Standard (DES), FIPS PUB 46-2,
6.2 b. Message Authentication Code (MAC), FIPS PUB 113, and
c. Key Management Using ANSI X9.17, FIPS PUB 171.

FIPS PUB 46-2 specifies a cryptographic algorithm that converts plaintext to ciphertext using a 56-bit key. Testing procedures for the validation of devices as conforming to FIPS PUB 46-2 are described in the NBS Special Publication 500-20, Validating the Correctness of Hardware Implementations of the NBS Data Encryption Standard . The validation of a device is performed by running the Monte Carlo test described in the publication. The Monte-Carlo test consists of eight million encryptions and four

million decryptions, with two encryptions and one decryption making up a single test. The test is designed to use the Electronic Codebook Mode (ECB) of DES. Although the actual test described in NBS Special Publication 500-20 is the same test used to validate devices today, the procedures for administering the test have changed. Currently, the test is performed by the vendor using initial values supplied by NIST. The vendor uses the supplied information to run the Monte-Carlo test and sends the results to NIST.

FIPS PUB 113, Computer Data Authentication, specifies a Data Encryption Algorithm which may be used to detect unauthorized intentional and accidental modifications to data. This process is known as data authentication. The algorithm is based on DES and is used to authenticate an entire binary message. FIPS PUB 1 13 is compatible with ANSI X9.9 which provides methods for authenticating an entire binary message as well as all or parts of a message which are in a coded character format. Procedures for the validation of products which implement FIPS PUB 113 and ANSI X9.9 are described in NBS Special Publication 500-156, Message Authentication Code (MAC) Validation System: Requirements and Procedures.
FIPS PUB 171 adopts ANSI X9. 17 for Federal Government use. ANSI X9. 17, Financial Institution Key Management (Wholesale) provides procedures and protocols for the secure generation, distribution,

storage, entry, use and destruction of symmetric cryptographic keying material (e.g., DES). It provides key management solutions for a variety of operational environments, and as such, ANSI X9. 17 contains a number of options. FIPS PUB 171 specifies a particular set of options whenever keying material is distributed using the protocols of ANSI X9.17. Procedures for the validation of products which conform to a subset of the options selected in FIPS PUB 171 are described in the Key Management Validation System: Point-to-Point Validation System document which is available from the Manager of the Security Group (see Section 6.5).

To validate a product, a vendor should send a formal request for validation which includes a clear indication of the product to be tested. The request must also include the name, address, and telephone number of the person within the vendor’s organization who will be responsible for the validation testing. The request should be sent to:
Manager, Security Technology Group Computer Security Division National Computer Systems Laboratory Building 225, Room A216 National Institute of Standards and Technology

FIPS 177, Initial Graphics Exchange Specifications (IGES) defines a neutral file format for the exchange of product model data and representation among differing computer-aided design and computer-aided manufacturing (CAD/CAM) systems. FIPS 177 adopts the ASME/ANSI Y14.26M, IGES version 4.0.

A revision to FIPS 177-1 (announced in Federal Register, April 12, 1995) will adopt the ANSI/US PRO 100 IGES, version 5.2. In accordance with FIPS 177-1, CAD/CAM systems acquired for Federal use shall include an IGES preprocessor and postprocessor capability. FIPS 177-1 requires that IGES implementations offered to Federal agencies be tested using the NIST IGES validation test suite. Conformance testing of IGES implementations protects Federal investments by ensuring adherence to the IGES specification and maximizing the probability of successful exchange among systems which implement IGES. The NIST IGES test procedures and test suites are available from:
Project Leader, IGES Validation Tests National Institute of Standards and Technology Bldg 225, Room A266

The NIST IGES Validation Test service tests preprocessors and/or postprocessors for conformance to 7.1.2 either IGES 4.0, IGES 5.2, or MIL-D-28000, Class II. Preprocessors and postprocessors are tested separately, using different test suites. A certificate of validation is issued for those processors that have been tested and are considered to be in compliance with FIPS 177. A registered report without certificate is issued for those processors that have been tested but contain errors.
